reviewBoundary: Three complete junior fifteen-gap originals. Fictional film, tandem ride and family-recipe cases; all option meanings/contexts reviewed by same author, not independent calibration.

units.alignmentNote: One complete original fifteen-gap four-option passage, matching the recorded level response structure. No source prose copied.

materials.title: The backwards poster
materials.text:
For a school film, Milo painted a poster saying "Have you seen our bear?" It had a red ____1____ around its edge. The poster would appear in the opening shot.

When the camera image appeared on the classroom screen, the writing looked ____2____. Milo thought his lettering was wrong. He read the poster aloud. On the paper, the words were perfectly ____3____.

The tablet’s front camera preview showed a mirror image, the teacher explained. They checked a saved test clip rather than guessing from the ____4____. The recorded words were the right way round.

 He had almost ____5____ the whole poster to solve a problem that was only in the preview. His friend Jo held up a book with a printed title. In the preview, that title looked backwards too, giving them a simple ____6____.

They filmed the opening scene. Milo's character pinned up the poster and hurried away. Then a corner came loose and covered half the bear's face. They had to stop, but this time the trouble was ____7____, not an effect of the screen.

Jo added a stronger hidden clip. They checked that the clip would not fall into the walking route, then filmed ____8____. The poster stayed flat.

Later, the class watched the saved scene.  Two different problems had required two different ____9____. One had been solved by understanding the image; the other by ____10____ the poster.

Milo wrote "check the saved file" on their equipment list. Jo added "check the ____11____ too". The camera could show them a picture, but it could not ____12____ every loose corner. Before the next scene, they looked around the whole ____13____. This time, the delay was caused by the actor playing the missing bear: he had gone to get water without telling ____14____. Milo called him back. Some problems were easier to ____15____ than others.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A red border runs around an edge. Price/address are information and handle a grip, not the painted edge design.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The mirrored preview reverses writing. Wet/unfinished do not explain the readably finished paper; smaller is not reversal.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The words read normally on paper. Silent/cost/secret do not contrast with mirrored direction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: They test a saved clip rather than rely on the live preview. Music, brush and weather are not the misleading display.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: He nearly paints the poster again. Selling/losing/framing would not fix supposedly wrong lettering.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: A known printed title provides a comparison. Permission/payment/invitation do not test reversal.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A loose corner is a physical object problem. It is visible, not imaginary; music/history do not describe it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: They repeat the shot, again. Yesterday contradicts sequence, abroad unsupported and alone contradicts group filming.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Different problems need different solutions. Bears/teachers/colours are not the fixes distinguished next.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The clip secures the poster. Translating/reading/selling do not stop the corner falling.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The film set includes the actual props beyond the saved file. Menu/score/season do not name the filming environment to inspect.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: A camera cannot fix a loose prop. It can record/show/enlarge images, which are not physical repair.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: They survey the room, the whole filming space. Title/bear/sentence are individual content, not the surrounding setting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Anyone names an unspecified person who could be informed. Anything is not a person, himself does not notify the others and without telling nobody gives a nonstandard negative combination here.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Calling the actor back solves the immediate absence. Hiding/painting/selling do not name correcting a production problem.

materials.title: The bicycle with two seats
materials.text:
My sister Bea chose the front seat of our hired two-seat bicycle. She knew the park. I was happy to sit behind until I discovered that I could not ____1____ where we went.

The hire-shop assistant explained. Bea would steer and use the brakes. We would both pedal, and we needed to ____2____ before starting or stopping. 

I pushed before Bea was ready, and she stopped us. "Tell me first," she said. I had treated two sets of pedals as two ____3____ machines, although they belonged to one bicycle.

We tried a countdown. This time, the start felt much ____4____. Bea named turns before we reached them. I told her when I needed to adjust my foot.

At a fork in the path, Bea called "left", then turned right. I stopped pedalling in ____5____. "My other left," she said. We laughed. We pulled safely off the path to check the ____6____ rather than argue while moving.

 We agreed to follow the signs and leave the shortcut for another day. Being familiar with a place did not mean Bea could not make a ____7____.

Our parents asked who had done more work. I could not give a useful ____8____. Bea had controlled the direction, but she could not feel exactly when my foot slipped. I had pedalled behind, but I could not ____9____ the front brake.

We had not become good at riding by doing the same job. We had learned to ____10____ the different information each seat provided. The final lap felt like a shared ____11____. We no longer needed a countdown: Bea asked whether I was ready, I answered, and we moved ____12____. I asked to hire it again. Bea agreed if I would not say "my other left" at every ____13____. I promised. Then I pointed towards the bus stop and immediately chose the wrong ____14____. Some jokes, apparently, are difficult to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The rear rider cannot steer/control direction. Remember/describe/enjoy do not identify the control missing from the second seat.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: They must communicate before coordinated changes. Racing/payment/singing do not supply the safety coordination.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: He acts as though pedals belonged to separate machines. They are not broken, and weight/rental is not the mistaken independence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Countdown coordination makes the start smoother. Noise/age/temperature do not describe that improved transition.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The unexpected wrong turn causes surprise. Advance/secret/return do not name his response.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: They check the map to settle their route. Brake/price/weather do not show the correct lake path.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Familiarity does not prevent a wrong-direction mistake. Profit/promise/repair are not the navigation error.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: More work asks for a comparison between contributions. Ticket/address/warning do not compare effort.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The rear rider cannot operate the front brake. Appearance/purchase/description are not physical control.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Cooperation combines different information. Erasing/hiding/selling would not integrate it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The enjoyable shared ride is an activity. It is no longer a contest/argument and is not secret or an accident.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: They coordinate and move together. The alternatives conflict with time, location or joint movement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The direction joke would recur at every turn. Meals/windows/lessons are not the route decisions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Pointing the wrong way chooses a wrong direction. Bicycle/sister/ticket are not what the gesture gets wrong.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: Difficult to escape means the recurring joke follows them. Drawing/buying/measuring do not express avoiding that recurrence.

materials.title: The mark beside the recipe
materials.text:
Sorting recipe cards with his aunt, Daniel found a brown-stained one. The ingredients were still readable, but half the final instruction was ____1____. His aunt recognised her father’s cake recipe.

Daniel offered to copy the recipe onto a clean card. He would not ____2____ the missing instruction. His aunt could not recall the baking time.

A relative’s birthday photograph showed the fruit-covered cake. That helped identify the finished ____3____, but it did not reveal how long it had been baked.

Next, they found a second version of the recipe in an old notebook. Its list of ingredients was slightly different, so they could not assume the instructions were ____4____. They recorded the differences.

Daniel's aunt decided to try the notebook version, which was complete. They followed appropriate food-safety instructions rather than guessing from the ____5____ card. The taste recalled family birthdays, without being exactly the same.

Daniel copied the complete version, noting its source, and photographed the marked card. The brown patch was not useful cooking information, but the card itself was part of the family's ____6____. A clean copy did not need to ____7____ it.

They placed both records in the box. One was ready to use; the other still held an unanswered question. Daniel had expected to finish with a single perfect ____8____. Instead, he had learned that two records could serve different ____9____.

A week later, his cousin sent a message. She remembered the brown mark being made when a mug fell at a family party. Nobody could ____10____ that memory from the card alone, so Daniel added it as her recollection, not a proven fact. It made the object more ____11____ without filling the missing line. The family could enjoy the story and still be ____12____ about its source. He left space for further notes. The box was tidier now, but its history was not ____13____. Someone might yet find another photograph or ____14____. Until then, the missing words would remain ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The brown mark covers the missing part. No translation/repetition/publication explains lost visibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: He avoids inventing the missing instruction. Copying/photographing/reading would preserve existing evidence, not fabricate absent words.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: A photo shows appearance. It cannot reveal oven timing/temperature, exact weight or price.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Different ingredients mean instructions cannot be assumed identical. Illegibility/secrecy/modernity are not the comparison at issue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The stained incomplete card is damaged. The alternative notebook is complete; digital/unused do not describe the source of the missing line.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The original card preserves family history. Shopping/budget/timetable are not its inherited significance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: A usable clean copy need not replace/displace the original. Explanation/description/photography can coexist and are not the deletion avoided.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: He expected one definitive answer/version. An ingredient, relative or camera is not the resolved result sought.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Use and historical preservation are different purposes. Colours/families/prices do not name the two functions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The card alone cannot confirm the cousin’s memory. Writing/sharing are possible without proof and forgetting is not verification.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: The recollection adds interest, while not completing or verifying the card. No value/price evidence is supplied.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: They can be clear about the source/qualification. Silent would withhold it; careless/angry do not express explicit provenance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: History remains open to further evidence, not finished. Visibility/location/personal nature do not contrast with future additions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Another notebook could supply written recipe evidence like the first. An oven/cake/cup is not a record likely to restore the line by itself.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The absent words remain unknown until evidence appears. Taste/popularity/printing do not describe their unresolved content.
